**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.5.0](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.5.0).

This is the third beta of 0.5.1. Since beta.2 it reworks how scenery tiles are built and cached: **a tile no longer keeps a magenta square after a bad answer from the imagery server, distant scenery is no longer too dark, and tiles are built faster.** It also retunes the **`network.connections`** levels, fixes several cache and configuration commands, and keeps game overlays such as MangoHud out of XEarthLayer. If you tested beta.2, see "Coming from beta.2" below.

0.5.1's biggest change is on macOS: **XEarthLayer no longer uses macFUSE's kernel extension.** It mounts its scenery through macFUSE's FSKit backend instead, so a new Mac no longer has to boot into Recovery and lower its security. On every platform, night lighting draws **street lamps along real roads**, cities are lit closer to what you see from the air, and **`network.connections`** keeps XEarthLayer from overwhelming home routers.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS 15.4 or newer, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-arm64-macos.pkg`, Homebrew (below), or `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` downloads are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

XEarthLayer is now licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. Releases up to beta.2 remain available under MIT. Nothing changes in how it works.

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. macOS only: set up macFUSE for FSKit

This build needs **macOS 15.4 or later** and **macFUSE 5.3.3 or later**. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.1/docs/macos.md) walks through each step.

1. Install or update [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io). If you already have 5.3.3 or later, keep it.
2. Open **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions**, click the ⓘ next to **File System Extensions**, and turn on **macFUSE (local)**. System Settings may list both **macFUSE** and **macFUSE (local)**; XEarthLayer needs **macFUSE (local)**.
3. If X-Plane is on an **external drive** (under `/Volumes`):
   - Give `/usr/libexec/fskitd` Full Disk Access under **Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access** (click **+**, press `Cmd+Shift+G` and type the path).
   - The drive must have ownership turned on. XEarthLayer checks this when it starts, and if ownership is off it stops and prints the `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` command for your drive.

Coming from 0.5.0? You no longer need the kernel extension you approved for it. Steps 1 and 2 are still needed: the kernel extension approval does not turn on the file system extension.

### 2. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.3
```

**macOS**, choose **one** of the three ways below.

**With the installer package.** Download `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-arm64-macos.pkg`, double-click it and follow the Installer. It puts `xearthlayer` in `/usr/local/bin`, which is already on your `PATH`. The package is signed and notarized with the ticket attached, so it installs without a network connection. In a new terminal:

```bash
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.3
```

**With Homebrew.** The pre-release channel follows every alpha, beta and rc build:

```bash
brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.3
```

If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`. Already on the channel? `brew upgrade --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease` is all you need.

**From the tarball.** Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you (`cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-arm64-macos`); with any other browser, `cd ~/Downloads` and `tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.3-arm64-macos.tar.gz`. Then:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.3
```

If `xearthlayer --version` prints something else, an older copy comes first on your `PATH`: `which -a xearthlayer` lists every copy.

### Coming from beta.1 or beta.2?

Install the binary (step 2), then bring the configuration up to date:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

It removes `texture.format`, which no longer exists: XEarthLayer encodes BC1 only, and choosing BC3 never produced usable scenery. A configuration that still has the line loads as before. Then read "After upgrading" below and go to step 5.

### 3. Coming from 0.5.0 or a 0.5.0 preview?

Your configuration and packages carry over. Bring the configuration up to date:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

It adds the new `[network]` section and removes `fuse.macos_backend` and `texture.format`, which no longer exist. Then read "After upgrading" below and go to step 5.

**One default changes for everyone:** `network.connections` is `high`, so XEarthLayer now opens a fifth fewer connections than 0.5.0 did. If you have prosumer or enterprise network hardware and want 0.5.0's limits back, `xearthlayer config set network.connections max`. See "What we most want tested" below.

### 4. New to XEarthLayer, or coming from v0.4.8?

Run `xearthlayer setup`. It asks for the network connections level as step 4: **High** suits most home routers, **Max** needs prosumer or enterprise network hardware, and **Low** is for older or low spec routers. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager, where you install the regions you fly (press `2` for the Library, mark regions with `Space`, press `i`).

Coming from v0.4.8, follow the upgrade steps in the [v0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.5.0) first: the rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the old packages must be removed before new ones are installed.

### After upgrading

From beta.1, beta.2 or 0.5.0:


- **Settings are checked when XEarthLayer starts.** A value in `config.ini` outside its range, for example from editing the file by hand, now stops XEarthLayer with a message naming the setting and its range, instead of being used as written. Correct it as the message says. `prefetch.box_extent = 6.5`, an old default, is read as 7.0, and `config upgrade` rewrites it.
- **The first start downloads some imagery again.** Downloaded imagery is now kept per imagery provider, and the old shared imagery cache is deleted in the background the first time XEarthLayer starts. Tiles already built stay in the cache; only a tile that has to be built again downloads its imagery again.
- **Tiles already in the cache keep their slightly darker distant levels** until the cache replaces them, so for a while a new tile beside an old one may look very slightly brighter at long range. To rebuild every tile at once, run `xearthlayer cache clear`, which now deletes only the cache.
- Night lighting saved on disk by beta.1 or beta.2 stays valid.

### 5. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## What changed since beta.2

**Scenery tiles**

- **No more magenta squares that stay.** When the imagery server, or a proxy, CDN or captive portal in between, answered with something that was not an image, such as an error page, the answer was saved to the cache and the tile kept a magenta square until `xearthlayer cache clear`. Such answers are now retried and never saved, a tile with any unusable piece is shown but not kept, and bad pieces already in the cache are removed the first time they are used.
- **Distant scenery is no longer too dark.** Each smaller version of a texture, which X-Plane draws in the distance, came out slightly darker than the one above it, by up to four and a half brightness steps at the smallest. They now keep the brightness of the tile.
- **A tile that finishes just as X-Plane stops waiting for it is kept**, so the next request for it is a fast cache hit rather than a second download and encode.
- **The first tile timeout no longer stalls other requests.** The magenta texture served for a tile that could not be made in time is built at startup, in a few milliseconds, instead of on first use.
- **Tiles are built faster**: imagery is decoded straight into the form the tile needs (about 43 ms down to 31 ms per tile), the smaller versions of each texture are built about twice as fast, and each texture is encoded into one buffer of exactly its size. The tiles are byte for byte the same as before apart from the brightness fix.

**Network**

- **`network.connections` levels retuned from field testing**: `high` (the default) now opens 80% of `max`, and `low` 65%. In beta.2 they opened two thirds and one third.

**Cache and configuration**

- **Each imagery provider keeps its own downloaded imagery.** After switching provider, a tile built again could be made from the previous provider's imagery, or a mix of both with visible seams.
- **`xearthlayer cache clear` deletes only the cache.** It deleted everything in the cache directory, the scenery indexes and the package manager's downloads included. It now refuses while `xearthlayer run` or a package operation is running. `xearthlayer cache stats` counts per provider and tier.
- **`xearthlayer run --no-cache` and `--no-prefetch` work.** Both only changed the startup message. `--no-cache` now runs the session without the disk cache (prefetch is off with it), and `--no-prefetch` turns prefetch off.
- **Settings outside their range are refused** when `config.ini` is read, by the same rule as `xearthlayer config set` (see "After upgrading").
- **A `config.ini` that cannot be read is no longer replaced with defaults.** `config set`, `init` and other commands saved the defaults over the whole file, losing every other setting. They now stop and name the file and the setting to correct.

**Night lighting**

- **Night textures just generated stay in memory.** Once the memory cache was full, a texture just generated could be dropped at once and generated again a few seconds later.

**GPU (Linux)**

- **Game overlays such as MangoHud no longer run inside XEarthLayer.** With MangoHud turned on for the whole system (`MANGOHUD=1`), its overlay ran inside XEarthLayer whenever it looked for GPUs and could abort it with `double free or corruption`. XEarthLayer now tells the Vulkan loader not to load such layers, unless you set `VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE` yourself.

**Removed**

- **BC3 texture compression, `texture.format` and `run --dds-format`.** Choosing BC3 never produced usable scenery, only magenta placeholders.

## What changed since 0.5.0

Everything under "What changed since beta.2" above, and:

**macOS**

- **No kernel extension.** XEarthLayer mounts through macFUSE's FSKit backend only. There is no Recovery step and no kernel extension approval, and the `fuse.macos_backend` setting is gone.
- **External drives.** At startup, XEarthLayer checks that the drive holding X-Plane honours ownership, and recreates its mount folder if it is empty, because FSKit refuses a folder made while ownership was off. A failed mount now names the likely causes rather than only macFUSE's `os error 35`.
- **Quitting leaves nothing mounted.** `q`, Ctrl+C and SIGTERM unmount the scenery, and a Ctrl+C during the first seconds of startup now does too (on Linux as well).
- **`xearthlayer diagnostics` has a macFUSE section**: the macFUSE version, whether its FSKit framework is present, and XEarthLayer's volume while it runs. The flight log records the same once after mounting.

**Night lighting**

- **Roads light up at night.** Motorways and main roads carry chains of street lamps, read from the road overlays and airport packs X-Plane loads in your `scenery_packs.ini` order, X-World Pro included. An area with no road overlay has no road lights, as it has no roads in the simulator.
- **Close to the aircraft, X-Plane's lights take over.** The lit layer fades to a quarter of its light as you close in and then leaves the ground beneath you to X-Plane's 3D lights.
- **Cities are whiter.** Most neighbourhoods are now LED white, the remaining sodium districts a softer amber, and distant towns keep their light and colour instead of fading to orange.
- Night lighting saved on disk by 0.5.0 is generated again the first time it is needed, so the first night flight in each area does more work.

**Network**

- **`network.connections` (`max`, `high`, `low`)** sets how many connections XEarthLayer opens: for imagery X-Plane is waiting on, for prefetch, kept open to the imagery servers, and for package downloads. The default is `high`.

**Dashboard**

- The headless status line, the panic report and the telemetry summary count the tiles being generated right now. The count was always 0, and it now reads "running".
- The Prefetch pane's meter is labelled **Utilization** and has a twelve-second sparkline.
- On Linux, "Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified" no longer appears over the dashboard when the shell has a stale `DISPLAY`.

## What we most want tested

### 1. `network.connections` on your network

The levels changed again from field testing: `high` opens 80% of `max`, `low` 65%.

- If XEarthLayer ever made your router, modem or Wi-Fi drop out, try `high` (the default) and then `low`, and tell us your router model and which level stays stable.
- On a fast connection with capable equipment, tell us whether `high` loads scenery noticeably slower than `max`, for example at the first scene load or a boundary crossing.

### 2. Scenery tiles

- **Magenta squares.** Do you still see magenta squares, and do any stay after X-Plane loads the area again? A square that comes and goes on a bad connection is expected; one that stays is a bug. The flight log has a `Tile incomplete` warning naming each tile that was served with missing imagery.
- **Distant terrain.** Does terrain in the distance look right against terrain closer in, after `xearthlayer cache clear` or on tiles built fresh? Screenshots help, with the location.
- **Scene loads and boundary crossings.** Do they feel as fast as beta.2 or faster?

### 3. The first start after upgrading

- Did the first start, with the old shared imagery cache being deleted in the background, run normally?
- Does `xearthlayer cache stats` show your providers and tiers, and does `xearthlayer cache clear` leave your packages, the scenery indexes and anything else you keep in the cache directory alone?
- If XEarthLayer refused to start over a setting, was the message clear?

### 4. macOS: FSKit from start to finish

If you have not yet tested it on a Mac, set up macFUSE as in step 1, then tell us:

- Did the steps work as written, especially turning on **macFUSE (local)**? Did anything ask for approval that the notes do not mention?
- Does `xearthlayer run` mount and serve scenery, and does `xearthlayer diagnostics` show `Mounted: FSKit` while it runs?
- With X-Plane on an external drive: did the Full Disk Access step and the ownership check behave as described?
- Quit with `q`, with Ctrl+C, and once during startup. Afterwards, `mount | grep zzXEL` should print nothing.

### 5. Night flights and your normal flights

Fly your usual routes, by day and by night, and tell us about anything that would stop you recommending this build: pauses or purple tiles at DSF boundary crossings, slow starts, missing scenery, road lamps where there is no road, or SimHeaven X-World Pro misbehaving with `packages.xworld_pro` on.

## How to report

The flight log is `xearthlayer.log`, and the package manager's log is `xearthlayer-packages.log`, both at `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS unless you changed `logging.file`. `xearthlayer run` empties the flight log when it starts, so copy it before the next flight. Then run:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the flight log, and what looked wrong. For a network report, include your router or modem model, your connection speed, and the `Network connections` line near the top of the flight log.

**On macOS, if the mount fails**, macFUSE's own message (`os error 35`) rarely says why. The reason is in the system log; run this right after the failure and include its output:

```bash
/usr/bin/log show --last 5m --predicate 'process == "fskitd"'
```

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**Distant levels of tiles cached before beta.3 are slightly darker** than those of new tiles until the cache replaces them. `xearthlayer cache clear` rebuilds them all.

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Saving a setting rewrites `config.ini` from its template.** Comments you added to the file by hand are lost, as they are with `xearthlayer config set`. The values are kept.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
